learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Understand mathematical language and symbology.
Know the different classes of numbers, especially real numbers.
Acquire skills in handling inequalities, absolute value, and bounds.
Know how to combine different techniques for calculating limits in one and several variables.
Understand the relationship between function continuity and open, closed, connected, and compact sets.
Know and interpret the concepts of directional derivative, partial derivative, and differential, as well as the relationships between them.
Manage the chain rule and its repercussions in relation to changes of variables and implicit differentiation.
Solve unconstrained local optimization problems.
Solve global optimization problems on compact sets.
Understand the underlying ideas in the construction of the Riemann integral and its applications.
Know the existence of improper and parametric integrals.
Visualize and represent regions in two and three dimensions and their transformations using polar, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates.
Know how to calculate double and triple integrals over simple regions.
Understand the underlying ideas in the definition of integrals over curves and surfaces.
Know the classical theorems of line and surface integrals as well as their relationship with classical differential operators.
Understand the concept of a numerical series and its convergence.
Know the power series expansion of some elementary functions.
Have an elementary knowledge of the complex exponential and Fourier series.

syllabus_topics: Part I: Functions of one and several variables. Limits and continuity
Part II: Differential calculus in several variables and applications

assessment_methods.method: Theory and Problems Exam (Special October Call)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary and extraordinary calls in January, students can choose to take only specific parts. The evaluation components are: First Partial Exam (4 points), Second Partial Exam (3.5 points), Practical Exam (2 points), and an Extra Test Question which substitutes workshop attendance (0.5 points). Incorrect multiple-choice answers subtract points for that specific section, but a negative total for a section is counted as zero. For the special October call, the theory and problems exam accounts for 8 points (2.5 hours) and the practical part accounts for 2 points (1 hour in a computer lab). No electronic devices like calculators or watches are allowed during the theory and problems exam; notes and USB drives are allowed for practical exams, but not internet access.
